answers.answer: Roll one die simultaneously for each held office card and add one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman also adds one. Modified 1–2 does nothing, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the member. Move the retiring member to Pensioners, flip that office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal attrition rolls.

Only players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard a London Season display card. They act in descending order of actual total retirement spending; ties go to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. A player may peek at display blackmails while acting. Do not refill cards while players select; if the display empties, skip every remaining eligible player. At the end discard every card still displayed and refill exactly three cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected one. Return all unused Pensioners to their supplies.

At the start of the Family phase, check the opportunity marker's location. Choose a main action once, or you may take it twice if the marker already matched that action at phase start; then move the marker onto the chosen action. Afterward, only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action; that action is not doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices and the marker already on Enlist Writer, taking Enlist Writer twice places three writers total: the vacancy bonus adds one writer once this turn, not once per repetition.
answers.evidence: Family action steps; Enlist Writer row

answers.answer: After all family actions, while both Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. A piece in Court is a Company share. If no Debt remains, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. Seeking a share places an applicant in an empty Stock Exchange queue space and pays its listed cost (£2, £3, £3, £4, or £5) to the bank; it does not pay family cash into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: Family—Seek Share and New Company shares

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order by the number on their card backs. The designated hirer chooses a candidate; the candidate moves into the office and its owner takes the office card. When promoting an officeholder, transfer that officeholder's fatigue to the new card and put the old card, now vacant, into ascending hiring order. Ordinary hiring of a member from the hirer's own family requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman first announces how many shares make a pure majority (more than half the current shares). Shareholders may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. Move one of the winner's Company shares into the Chairman slot and give them the title marker. If no candidate receives majority support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself, without Nepotism consent. The Chairman piece still counts as a Company share for dividends, majority, and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in a firm.

First commit resources and any cash: all cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll; use the lowest die. A 1–2 succeeds. A 3–4 fails, but can be retried if resources and office-specific limits allow. A 5–6 is catastrophic: the office takes no further actions, its holder returns to supply, fatigue is discarded, and the card flips into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander and firm procedures can modify this. Do not take an action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice merely to trigger possible officer losses.

The Chairman may freely add up to three Debt, receiving £5 Balance for each. Each additional advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counting toward that majority. Borrowing must never move beyond the Debt track end. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; the Chairman may interleave borrowing and allocation while observing the borrowing limits. Cash already in office treasuries remains there for those offices to use.

The Manager of Shipping must spend treasury funds until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Leased extra ships remain only until Refresh.

For a Trade action, declare the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success, fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions: place the first writer at the home port, then each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use physical writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A President may never fill another President's home region, even if that other office is vacant. Increase Company Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it earlier that turn under Deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order, and each writer owner receives £1 per writer placed. A President can have at most one successful Trade per turn; failed attempts/retries remain within its uninterrupted opportunity.

A Commander may Deploy against their Presidency's home region, any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home region or another Presidency's Company-controlled region; a Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have an effect. Exhaust chosen officers and regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice. Subtract the combined strength of the target and all other regions in its empire, counting the target once; Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll for officer losses.

On a successful Deploy, take bank loot equal to £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot modifier, with a minimum equal to the number of surviving officers used in that attempt plus one. Distribute it in repeated cycles: first the Commander family gets £1 for the Commander and £1 for each of its used surviving officers; then other families clockwise get £1 per used surviving officer; last the bank gets £1 per used regiment and per used local-alliance piece. Repeat until all loot is distributed or cash runs out. The Commander also takes one trophy per target tower. Then remove the target tower/dome, remove all matching empire flags if the target was a capital, open all its orders and clear unrest. If it becomes Company-controlled, put its loot/control token region-side above the President, place the Governor overlay there, and put only the office card in Vacant Offices; if the Elephant pointed outward from the conquered region, move it fully inside. On catastrophe, the Commander returns half their family's trophies, rounded up, and the Commander returns to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and there is no Commander office card to vacate.

A Governor takes the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduces the pool by one regardless of result. On success the Governor takes £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then chooses exactly one benefit: a Build (two successful Builds create a partial ship in the Governor's region, then complete it into the associated President's sea zone); commission a regiment into that President's Army; or Tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury. Every unsuccessful roll adds one unrest in the region; catastrophe also removes the officeholder under the normal rule. Each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest. Repeat with the shrinking pool until choosing to stop, no dice remain, or catastrophe occurs.

At Revenue expenses, reduce Balance by £1 per existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in sea zones (including China); exclude Commanders. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one space per loan until the track ends; continue taking emergency loans even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt adds no expense this turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two loans reduce Standing one; three or more reduce it two. Then compare the remaining Balance with expectations at current Standing; if it is below expectations, reduce Standing one. Finally, the Chairman may pay any affordable number of dividends, each costing one cash per Company share and paying each owner £1 per share, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one. Company failure occurs if Standing reaches its leftmost space.

An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary attack first, then secondary regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; each Commander orders attacks within their Presidency. A normal primary Crisis attacks at its normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in the target. A primary Foreign Invasion uses only its ordinary attack die, with no added unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that region, with no modifier or empire strength. The associated Commander must exhaust active Army pieces totaling that strength, or as much as possible, using local alliances at printed strength and never splitting an alliance. If defense strength is insufficient, apply Region Loss. If sufficient, clear all unrest in that attacked region and give the Commander one trophy; if this successful defense defeated a normal primary Invasion, also remove one tower from the attacking region if possible. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts instead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses pieces but gains or loses no trophies. This does not appoint a Commander.

The PM reveals up to three laws one at a time, chooses one and discards the others; drawing a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing. The PM chooses a direction around the dial, stopping at the first policy space matching the law's bottom icon, then chooses that policy's target and consequence and sets Vote to the law's printed starting support. Starting with the PM and moving clockwise, players vote using £1 family cash per vote plus printed card votes (rotate used cards); support can move without limit. The PM may call another full round or stop after a round; a round with no votes ends voting. A player who voted for may later oppose, but after opposing cannot vote for during that vote. The PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except when forced by the specified promise. Support of −1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, give the Opposition Leader the PM dial, and have the new PM move the proposed policy one space either direction and resolve that adjacent policy. At support zero or higher, the law passes: place it with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first and then the law's immediate effects. Finally restore voting cards to their regular orientation after either result. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.

In 1758 and Long 1710, at the very start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. Passing lowers Debt by one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives the PM a passed-law token, and activates firms. Failure raises Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing the Court VP token, up to a maximum of ±3. No policy accompanies this vote; failure neither removes the PM nor discards the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. Scenario 1813 starts deregulated.

After Family share creation and before Hiring, players may take firm investment actions until no one wishes more. To form a firm, a player who manages no firm returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips their family board, places a family member as the first firm share, sets Value to the leftmost track space, and takes £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. An investment, with manager consent, contributes a Company share or workshop the same way and adds £5 bank cash to London; it creates a firm share unless the firm already has ten, in which case the contribution still adds £5 but creates no share. The Chairman's share cannot be used, shares created this turn cannot be used even if traded away, and no Company share can be invested while Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space. Invested workshops never revert to uninvested and get neither workshop bonuses nor Company-failure VP, even if the firm fails.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers simultaneously and secretly choose a trade zone/home port (requires at least one ship and permits a closed home port) and commit a secret cash bid from London, or choose Hobnob (no bid, trade, or dividends; expenses still apply and the previous dividend marker remains). Reveal bids together but keep strategies facedown until the matching Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before actions, reveal matching strategies; roll one die per committed £1 and pay the bid to the bank. At least one 1 or 2 permits trade. Firm initiative is ship count minus successful dice (1s/2s), possibly negative; a successful President Trade generates initiative by the same method using Presidency ships. After the President's successful trade, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President chooses among ties. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders/Governors, with the Chairman breaking initiative ties. A firm fills open orders up to ships plus one, starting at its strategy home port and tracing its route through its own filled orders; it may fill each order only once, but can refill an order another firm or the Company filled this turn, and the Company can refill a firm's. A previously filled order pays half printed revenue, rounded down. Firm Value advances one space per full £6 added to its India treasury that turn.

At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order, then other firms; ties go to the manager with the most windows, then PM clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. If a firm cannot pay, it dissolves unless rescued: its shares go to Debtor's Prison for −1 VP each, ships return to shipyards, its charter returns to family side, and contributed workshops stay invested. It may be rescued by emergency investments under normal Company-share/workshop rules (the firm pays expenses, loses remaining cash, and lowers Value one space per emergency investment) or by merging with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not yet paid and cover the endangered firm's unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends only from India treasury; each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager. With manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment for any number of their shares on a dividend. Record total actual cash paid, not the per-share rate, on the dividend marker; an active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero, while Hobnob retains its old marker. Sweep remaining India funds into London.
